<action type="say">
What you’re describing is very plausible: if you’re actively using a University of Alabama Credit Union debit card for groceries, there *is* a transaction account behind it (almost certainly a checking), even if it’s not showing on your online “Accounts” page.

Most likely scenarios:
- The checking account tied to your debit card is not linked to your current online banking profile, or
- It’s mis-classified or hidden in the system view you’re seeing.

Here’s how to approach this with the credit union as efficiently as possible.

1) Grab these details before you contact them
- Your debit card:
  - Last 4 digits of the card number
  - Expiration date
- Any old checkbook from them (if you have one): last 4 digits of the account number
- Your member number (often shown next to “Primary Share” or “Member Savings” online)

2) What to say when you call or send a secure message
You can copy/paste or read this almost verbatim:

“Hi, I’m logged in to online banking on my laptop. Under Accounts I only see ‘Primary Share’ and ‘Member Savings.’ However, I’ve been using my University of Alabama Credit Union debit card ending in [last 4 digits] regularly for years. I believe that card is tied to a checking account, but I don’t see any checking account listed online.  

Can you please:
1) Look up which account this debit card is linked to,  
2) Confirm the account type and status, and  
3) Make sure that account is visible on my online banking profile so I can see my balance and transactions?”

If they say the debit card is tied to a checking, explicitly add:
- “Great, please enable that checking to display in my online banking under Accounts. Right now, I can’t see its balance at all.”

If they say it’s tied to something unexpected (like a share draft/share account):
- “Whatever account this debit card is drawing from — I need that account to appear in my online banking so I can see the balance and transactions.”

3) After they fix it
Once they confirm they’ve linked/unhidden it, log out of online banking, close the browser tab, and log back in. Your checking (or whatever they call it) should then appear, and your current/available balance will be visible.

If you’d like, tell me:
- The last 4 digits of the debit card (only the last 4, nothing else),
- Any labels you see in online banking that look like “cards,” “debit,” or “plastic,”

and I can help you phrase an even more specific message (or check that what they tell you on the phone makes sense). </action>
